description: R06-A host/ConPTY source reconciliation. Exact entries use Microsoft-derived vectors against migrated Rust product APIs; source rules remain conservative where C++ aggregate, Win32, ICU, queue, iterator, or screen-buffer behavior is not owned end-to-end by Rust.

entries.notes: Same Microsoft pangram; one narrow output cell per UTF-16 code unit with Current attribute behavior.
Same five Katakana codepoints; each emits Leading then Trailing without double-consuming input.
Same Microsoft pangram with Stored text-attribute behavior across every cell.
Same five full-width Katakana glyphs with Stored attributes on both leading and trailing cells.
Same pangram and equal input/cell distance for narrow text.
Same QWER + five Katakana + TYUI shape; cell distance exceeds input distance by five trailing cells.
All Microsoft equal/left/right/above/below/diagonal row-major comparison cases are reproduced against BufferPoint ordering.
Same four coordinates and concatenated CUP bytes.
Same plain title, C0 controls, DEL and C1 control vectors through migrated sanitizer plus OSC-0 framing.
Same 16 foreground, 16 background and two reverse-video legacy attribute vectors.
Rust TextBuffer does not yet own the C++ CopyRequest/GetPlainText block-selection extraction contract.
Rust TextBuffer does not yet own wrapped-line trimming and CRLF projection for clipboard plain-text extraction.

sourceRules.notes: DOSKEY alias storage, macro expansion and executable-scoped lookup have no migrated Rust owner.

These methods assert full console API/global-state behavior: input modes, cooked reads, title/codepage conversion, waits, writes and screen-buffer scrolling. terminal-host does not own that aggregate yet.

The remaining clipboard methods depend on Win32 keyboard-layout mapping, AltGr/numpad synthesis and Win32 clipboard/input integration. The two portable-looking buffer extraction methods are explicitly kept Missing above.
Rust owns parsing after Windows tokenization plus client argument escaping. Microsoft methods begin from the raw command line and therefore still include CommandLineToArgvW/platform behavior.
CommandHistory allocation, reuse, resizing, duplicate policy and persistent session storage have no migrated Rust owner.
GetConsoleLangId is explicitly a Windows-loader/code-page compatibility contract over Windows LANGID values.
Input queue insertion, coalescing, flushing, peeking, wait-event signaling, DBCS padding, suspension and stream de-coalescing have not moved into Rust.
Console object handle allocation/share-count behavior and ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION remain Windows object/handle ownership.

Rust owns the text-backed iterator, width expansion, UTF-16 glyph grouping, stored attributes and cell limits. C++ attribute-only, CHAR_INFO, OutputCell-run and unlimited fill constructor surfaces are not all represented; six portable methods are promoted Exact above.

The 113-method screen-buffer aggregate spans cursor, viewport, renderer, selection, VT state, API mutation, reflow and platform coordination. No single safe Rust aggregate owns that contract yet, so similarity to lower-level crates is not used as parity evidence.
Console search remains dependent on the ICU-backed search adapter; this is the same explicit Unicode/search backlog identified in R04.

Rust owns deterministic selection spans and keyboard movement, while these host tests also depend on the legacy Selection singleton, console globals, cooked-read/history state and host TextBuffer integration.

These 29 contracts are specifically the C++ TextBufferCellIterator/TextBufferTextIterator operator API. Rust intentionally has different iteration mechanics and no direct product abstraction that can honestly witness this exact helper surface yet.

Rust owns rows, attributes, wide glyphs and core resize/reflow behavior, but Microsoft's host suite also asserts circular-buffer rotation, renderer/VT orchestration, API backspace/write paths, clipboard text extraction, hyperlinks and prompt-region behavior outside the current Rust owner.
TranslateConsoleTitle environment unexpansion and filesystem-title substitution have no migrated Rust owner; this is distinct from VtIo OSC title framing.
Fallback is intentionally Missing; the suite's sole TestCompareCoords method is explicitly Exact above.

Rust preserves exclusive/inclusive rectangle geometry used by viewports, but does not yet expose the full Viewport factory, bounds, clamp, convert, increment/decrement and compare API exercised by all 23 methods.

Rust owns deterministic VT sequence, sanitization, attribute and CHAR_INFO serialization logic; Microsoft also drives ApiRoutines, pipes and live screen-buffer mutation. Four pure byte-format contracts are promoted Exact above.
